newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Shell proposes $2.5 bln investment in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Shell proposes $2.5 bln investment in Bangladesh.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group has submitted a proposal to the Bangladesh government to build a $2.5 billion plant to convert natural gas into petroleum products, the company's office in Dhaka said on Thursday.
"We are projecting to produce at least 50,000 barrels a day. So, initially we can even export petroleum," Siraj-ud Dowla, managing director of the Shell Company of Bangladesh, told Reuters.
Dowla said the company would build the plant within two and one-half years if the proposal "if the proposal immediately gets government approval."
Shell said the project could eliminate Bangladesh's need to import refined petrolem products such as diesel fuel and kerosene for the next five to 10 years.
Bangladesh currently imports an average of 30,000 barrels of refined petroleum products a day.
An eight-member team of officials from Shell Exploration & Production International in Holland and London visited Bangladesh last week and made the proposal to energy ministry officials.
The team also discussed the proposal with Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, company officials said.
Bangladesh has proven gas reserves of 10.2 trillion cubic feet. Dowla said his company alone has discovered 12 fields, including Bangladesh's biggest, the Bakhrabad gasfield.
Bangladesh spends around $300 million annually on imports of refined petroleum products, officials said. Of this, Shell brands account for about $50 million a year.
Bangladesh's government does not subsidise petroleum product prices, officials said.
Two Shell representatives recently visited Bangladesh's southern districts of Khulna and Bhola, which are potential sites for the project.
Dowla told Reuters that Shell wanted to "return to Bangladesh in a big way."
The company has offered to explore and develop the Shahabazpur gas field in Bhola under a joint venture with the state-run petroleum corporation Petrobangla.
Shell also offered assistance with technical difficulties faced by the Bakhrabad gasfield being developed by Petrobangla, Dowla said.
Energy ministry officials said the government was considering Shell's proposal. "We welcome all investment proposals, especially from big companies," one official said without elaborating.
Officials said the U.S. oil company Unocal had recently also proposed working with Petrobangla to develop the Shahabazpur gasfield and set up a gas-fired power plant there.
